    Kutra (Owlkin)¶

    A species of humanoid owls native to the Demon Continent, inhabiting the Kutra Tribe territory across a river. Kutra do not breathe oxygen but can survive outside water for up to two days. They are capable of flight and possess a culture adapted to both aquatic and aerial environments.

    Biology¶

    • Appearance: Humanoid owls standing 1.5–1.8 meters tall. Feathered bodies with human-like arms ending in taloned hands. Large, forward-facing eyes adapted for both underwater and low-light vision. Feather coloring ranges from mottled brown to silver-gray
    • Respiration: Gills and lungs. Kutra breathe water through gill-slits along their ribs and air through lungs. They can switch between the two seamlessly
    • Flight: Silent flight — their feathers are structured to eliminate sound, making them nearly undetectable in the air
    • Lifespan: 60–80 years
    • Mage-cell expression: Low. Kutra mages are rare and typically specialize in water manipulation

    Society¶

    The Kutra Tribe builds settlements across and along the river — half the village above water, half below. Their architecture is amphibious: sleeping chambers are submerged (where they breathe water) while communal areas are above the surface.

    • Nation: Kutra Tribe (Demon Continent)
    • Governance: Dual chieftains — one for the river (below) and one for the sky (above). Major decisions require consensus between both
    • Culture: Silence is valued. Their language includes sign-gestures made with talons and wing-flicks. Speaking aloud is reserved for important declarations. Kutra children learn to sign before they learn to speak
    • Economy: River-trade — they ferry goods along the waterways of the Demon Continent, charging in rare river-gems found only in their territory
    • Relations: Respected by the Maomodor Kingdom and the Malgardian Tribe. The Asatru Empire maintains a trade embassy in their largest settlement

    Connections¶

    • Nation: Kutra Tribe (Demon Continent)
    • Traits: Humanoid owls, amphibious, silent flight, dual governance, sign-language culture
